info.album: Love Is Like Oxygen / Reach Out ... I'll Be There (Remastered)

podcast.body: Another hit by the glam band Sweet, mentioned as part of the body of work that ABBA initially considered emulating. "little Willie love is like oxygen."

This song demonstrates the band's transition from glam rock to metal, marking a significant shift from their earlier bubblegum sound. "Back in episode 20 of this podcast I talked about the British band Sweet and how their song Love is like oxygen shows the transition of glam rock to metal."

podcast.body: This song, released in 1978 when glam was waning, made it to number eight on the Billboard Pop Chart. The Edmonton Journal in 1998 ran a contest challenging readers to find "the worst unintentionally bad song lyrics" and used this song as an example. Andy Scott, the band's songwriter and lead guitarist, confirmed that the band was already "part rock, part metal" when he wrote it, intending to compose it in a new style that suited their evolving sound, signifying glam's transition into metal. "Love is like oxygen we can't so much, we can't too much, love is like oxygen."
